metadata.title: Brevyn Spann-Ford - Versatile in Week 1 loss
metadata.description: Spann-Ford caught both of his targets for 14 yards and made one tackle on kick coverage in Sunday's 28-20 loss to the Giants.
metadata.analysis: Spann-Ford is the No. 2 tight end behind Jake Ferguson, but the secondary option outperformed Ferguson by eight receiving yards in Sunday's contest. Spann-Ford played 13 offensive snaps and 11 special teams snaps, contributing to the Cowboys in both phases to the start the season.

metadata.title: Brevyn Spann-Ford inks extension with Cowboys
metadata.description: Brevyn Spann-Ford signed a three-year contract extension with the Cowboys on Thursday.
metadata.analysis: After originally signing as an undrafted free agent, Spann-Ford has played in 17 games each of the last two seasons for the Cowboys. He's not been much of a pass catcher, but the 26-year-old tight end has excelled as a blocker and special-teams contributor.

metadata.title: Brevyn Spann-Ford - Inks three-year extension
metadata.description: Spann-Ford signed a three-year extension with the Cowboys on Thursday, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
metadata.analysis: Spann-Ford has played in all 34 regular-season games with Dallas during his first two NFL seasons and is now set to remain with the club for the foreseeable future. The Minnesota product hasn't been a big part of the Cowboys' passing game, logging only 18 catches during those 34 contests, but he has contributed solid blocking in a rotational role. Spann-Ford should continue to work behind starter Jake Ferguson and alongside fellow reserve Luke Schoonmaker in 2026.

metadata.title: Brevyn Spann-Ford Agrees to Three-Year Extension with Cowboys
metadata.description: The Dallas Cowboys and tight end Brevyn Spann-Ford agreed to terms on a three-year extension on Thursday, per ESPN's Adam Schefter. Since catching on with Dallas as an undrafted free agent ahead of 2024, Spann-Ford has seen minimal usage as a pass-catcher through the first two years of his career. Across 17 games (five starts) in 2025, the 26-year-old recorded nine catches for 90 yards and one touchdown on 13 targets. Entering 2026, Spann-Ford is once again expected to be the blocking complement to Cowboys receiving tight ends Jake Ferguson and Luke Schoonmaker. Dallas' financial commitment to Spann-Ford proves that the team values his contributions, but he should remain off fantasy radars in 2026.

metadata.title: Brevyn Spann-Ford - Primed for backup role
metadata.description: Spann-Ford is expected to earn a spot on Dallas' tight end depth chart behind starter Jake Ferguson, Nick Harris of the Fort Worth Star-Telegram reports.
metadata.analysis: Spann-Ford appeared in all 17 games for the Cowboys for the second straight season in 2025, so it's reasonable to anticipate he'll play a role in the offense again in 2026. However, he spent most of his snaps last year blocking, so there's no guarantee an increased snap count would translate to fantasy reliability.

metadata.title: Brevyn Spann-Ford Expected to Operate in Backup Role
metadata.description: Dallas Cowboys tight end Brevyn Spann-Ford is expected to earn a spot on the 53-man roster in a backup role to top pass-catching TE Jake Ferguson in 2026, according to Nick Harris of the Fort Worth Star-Telegram. Spann-Ford has played in all 17 games in both of his two NFL seasons in Dallas since joining the team as an undrafted free agent out of the University of Minnesota. The 26-year-old has mostly been used as a blocker on offense, though, so he hasn't been on the fantasy football radar at all. He has had exactly nine receptions in each of his first two seasons, combining for 178 yards and just one touchdown reception in 34 games played (five starts). Spann-Ford had 90 receiving yards and a touchdown catch last year, which included all five of his career starts. If Ferguson were to miss time due to an injury, Luke Schoonmaker, not Spann-Ford, would likely be the better waiver-wire target as a streaming tight end in fantasy.

metadata.title: Brevyn Spann-Ford - Provides reliable depth at TE
metadata.description: Spann-Ford caught nine of 13 targets for 90 yards and his first career touchdown over 17 games for the Cowboys in 2025.
metadata.analysis: The second-year tight end has emerged as a dependable depth option, drawing excellent grades for his run blocking while also handling a regular role on special teams. Spann-Ford got rewarded for his work in the trenches with a four-yard TD pass from Dak Prescott in Week 12, but his usage as a pass rush catcher behind starter Jake Ferguson remains limited. Spann-Ford has one more year left on his rookie contract before becoming a restricted free agent, so he should fill a similar spot on the depth chart in 2026.

metadata.title: Brevyn Spann-Ford catches pass in Week 17
metadata.description: Brevyn Spann-Ford caught one of his two targets for 31 yards in the Cowboys' 30-23 win over the Commanders in Week 17.
metadata.analysis: Spann-Ford remains a non-factor in the Dallas offense, recording two targets or less in each of his 16 games. The tight end remains best left out of lineups in all formats ahead of a Week 18 contest against the New York Giants.

metadata.title: Brevyn Spann-Ford - Catches first career TD
metadata.description: Spann-Ford caught his only target for a four-yard touchdown in Sunday's 24-21 win over the Eagles.
metadata.analysis: The second-year tight end barely kept his balance after colliding with Andrew Mukuba to haul in his first career NFL touchdown on a designed rollout by Dak Prescott in the third quarter. Spann-Ford's role on offense remains limited -- he has yet to see more than one target in any game this season en route to a 5-22-1 line on six targets through 11 games -- and even if something were to happen to starter Jake Ferguson, Luke Schoonmaker (8-63-0 on 16 targets this season) might remain ahead of him on the depth chart.

metadata.title: Brevyn Spann-Ford - Notches fourth catch of season
metadata.description: Spann-Ford was on the field for 24 of the Cowboys' 67 snaps on offense and recorded a four-yard reception on his lone target in Monday's 33-16 win over the Raiders.
metadata.analysis: Spann-Ford once again served as Dallas' No. 3 tight end, with his 36 percent snap share placing him behind Jake Ferguson (63) and Luke Schoonmaker (45). The second-year player out of Minnesota now has four receptions for 18 yards on five targets through 10 appearances.
